{{Quote|Set out a suit of clothes, would you? Something I can wear outside, but it must make me look wonderful.|Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] to one of her [[Handmaiden/Legends|handmaidens]]|<ref name="DR">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>}}
'''Clothing''' referred to garments made from various types of materials and taking several forms used by [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings to cover their body. In addition to their protective functions, clothes were also worn for the socialization: on worlds such as [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] or [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], styles of clothes reflected all the strata of society. Beings would also wear such coverings out of modesty, hiding parts of their bodies that were considered private. From very early [[Time/Legends|times]], many sentient and semi-sentient [[Species/Legends|species]] used to wear clothes, including the [[Human/Legends|Humans]] or the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]]. Conversely, other species like the [[Tchuukthai]] or the [[Oswaft]] usually did not, either for natural or cultural reasons.

==Practical functions==
{{Quote|Let's get you some clean clothes and something to eat. You'll feel better then, I promise.|[[Ulu Ulix]] to [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]|<ref name="Crossfire">''[[Boba Fett: Crossfire]]''</ref>}}
[[File:HanParka-Hasbro.png|thumb|left|160px|Clothes could shield from cold and other severe weather conditions.]]
Pragmatically, clothes would protect from various kind of damage&mdash;including heat, cold, wind or dirt. On [[Star/Legends|sun]]-scorched and arid planets such as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], the inhabitants wore rough-spun tunics that could withstand the hostile weather, and often added leg and wrist bindings that kept out sand and dust.<ref name="TPMV" /> Such garments would protect them from sunburns and wind scars.<ref name="TLH">[[Star Wars Annual (1977) 1|''Star Wars Annual'' (1977) 1]]</ref> The [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibian]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] from [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] chose stretchy trousers with tight ends that allowed them to swim easily and kept out [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]] crawling creatures.<ref name="TPMV" /> Those who needed to protect themselves against the cold would simply put on heavy clothes and animal skins, or rely on technological garments such as insulated jumpsuits, self-warming headgears and heated [[parka]]s. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] that pitted the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], both belligerents used garments adapted to intense cold, with those garments coming in handy during the events surrounding the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].<ref name="SWV">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Certain types of clothes were specifically designed to protect the wearer from traumatic injuries. Heavy cloth woven with energy-absorbing fibers could serve as a shield against [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire, and various parts of a suit&mdash;notably the collar&mdash;could contain blast-absorbing paddings.<ref name="TPMV" />

[[File:Selonian_AA.jpg|thumb|160px|Members of the [[Selonian/Legends|Selonian]] species usually went naked.]]
While some [[Species/Legends|species]] generally covered all or most of their body parts, others only wore what was functionally required. [[Crystal/Legends|Crystalline]] or gas-based sentients had no need for clothes,<ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book) ">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> and most [[Hair/Legends|furry]] species like the [[Trianii/Legends|Trianii]] never wore anything more than [[Armor/Legends|armor]] or utility belts.<ref name="HSE">''[[Han Solo at Stars' End]]''</ref> On their native world, [[Togorian/Legends|Togorians]] seldom wore clothing, as the weather was mostly clement.<ref name="TPS">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref> The [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] from [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], who were known for their thick uniform coat of water-shedding hair,<ref name="ROSV">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> only wore clothes on special occasions, including the [[Life Day/Legends|Life Day]] celebration, which required the use of a ritual [[Life Day robes/Legends|red robe]].<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> The [[S'kytri]], a race of winged [[Near-Human]]s from [[Skye/Legends|Skye]], usually had few clothes due to their world's permanently warm [[Temperature/Legends|temperature]]. Additionally, too much material could generate wind resistance and hinder their flight, which is why S'kryti of all genders wore little else than slight coverings to protect their genitalia.<ref name="GM1">{{GamerCite|1|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Marvel Series}}</ref>

==Cultural significance==
===Social indicator===
{{Quote|There's more to the galaxy than elaborate dresses and fancy parties.|Princess Leia Organa|<ref name="The Princess Leia Diaries">{{Tales|11|The Princess Leia Diaries}}</ref>}}
[[File:Draped_Senator.png|thumb|left|180px|A Human [[Senator/Legends|senator]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] draped in a large sheet of mauve fabric.]]
Clothing was also used as an indicator of social status, [[Gender/Legends|gender]] or individual preferences. This was particularly true in societies based on individual competition; amongst the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]], elaborate clothes would strongly assert their wearer's wealth and social position over others.<ref name="TPMV" /> Even more precisely, the shapes of their cloaks, hats, drapes and collars each had a specific symbolic meaning, together with the fabric types and the color choices.<ref name="SON">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> High-ranking Neimoidians placed huge value on their headgears, and it was thought they would never be seen without one unless they were dead.<ref name="Hunt">''[[Boba Fett: Hunted]]''</ref> In fact, the Neimoidian clothing etiquette was so elaborated that the [[Republic Xenosociological Database]] contained a whole subdirectory dedicated to it.<ref name="SON" />

On [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], a world that remained the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] throughout many successive regimes, numerous extravagant fashion styles were displayed. Among the [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] and [[Senator/Legends|senators]], luxurious versions of the traditional costumes of hundreds of planets could be seen, as well as many styles particular to Coruscant.<ref name="TPMV" /> Patrons of the [[Galaxies Opera House/Legends|Galaxies Opera House]] often wore excessive dresses that had nothing to envy to the actors' stage costumes.<ref name="ROSV" /> Expensive outfit displayed a wide array of high-priced materials such as [[Tomuon]] wool,<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> [[Shimmersilk/Legends|shimmersilk]],<ref name="ROSV" /> and [[crosh-hide]].<ref name="VotF">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>

Despite the numerous cultural differences, many species throughout the galaxy shared a basic design of simple, loose-fitting robes, which inspired the humble [[Jedi apparel/Legends|Jedi apparel]].<ref name="TPMV" /><ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book) " /> However, although the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] rejected materialist preoccupations, their clothes were not considered uniforms, and the wearers were left some freedom to personalize them.<ref name="FF98">{{FactFile|98|GAR 5-6|Garments and Couture}}</ref> As such, the [[Jedi Lord]] [[Valenthyne Farfalla]] donned elaborate attires with gold and precious gems.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> In the three-year time span of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the notorious Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] had used only six robes.<ref name="ROSV" /> By adopting the traditional trappings of the Order, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Tyvokka/Legends|Tyvokka]] was one of the few Wookiees who would wear clothes on a regular basis.<ref name="SHW1">[[Star Wars (1998) 36|''Star Wars'' (1998) 36]]</ref> The [[Sith/Legends|Sith Order]] used [[Sith apparel|similar robes]], but in shades of black rather than brown.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" />

[[File:Elli_Stark_evening_gown.png|thumb|right|150px|[[Elli Stark]] wearing a revealing evening gown at the Imperial function on Etti IV.]]
On highly cultured planets such as Naboo, clothing was often used a form of social communication. For example, during the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]], the citizens of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] made subtle use of Naboo [[Color/Legends|color]] and fashion symbolism to express their support or opposition to the Queen [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala's]] policies.<ref name="TPMV" /> The [[Education Advisor|Education Regent]] of Naboo [[Lufta Shif/Legends|Lufta Shif]] wore gentle and flowing teaching robes, reflecting the belief that learning was best encouraged by inspiration rather brute force or threat.<ref name="FF139">{{FactFile|139|LUF 1-2|Lufta Shif}}</ref> The Queen herself wore clothes that made her look taller and larger through the use of wide shoulders and massive headpieces.<ref name="TPMV" /> In fact, the use of Naboo royal costume was highly codified and one of the most intricate in the galaxy.<ref name="FF104">{{FactFile|104|GAR 7-8|Garments and Couture}}</ref> On [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], one of the oldest colonies of Humans,<ref name="Illustrated">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> the design and style of the clothes were much simpler, with a predominance of white in the ambassadorial milieu.<ref name="CoPL">''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]''</ref> Among many humanoid species,<ref name="DVRL">''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader: A 3-D Reconstruction Log]]''</ref> including the Humans of [[Serenno/Legends|Serenno]],<ref name="AOCVD">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> wearing a [[Cape/Legends|cape]] was associated with power and nobility.<ref name="DVRL" />

===Clothing and modesty issues===
{{Quote|Nice outfit&mdash;what, you miners change regulation uniforms while I've been in here?|[[Atton Rand]], upon seeing [[Meetra Surik]] in her undergarment|<ref name="The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
In many species, wearing clothes was also a question of modesty, and appearing in the nude was considered indecent. In the majority of the [[galactic community]], it was customary to cover at least certain intimate body parts.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 90" /> Once, when [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] was forced to wear a dress that left the right side of her body exposed, the people attending the ceremony in which she took part stared at her in embarrassment.<ref name="SW95">[[Star Wars (1977) 95|''Star Wars'' (1977) 95]]</ref> Among the [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]], a people of [[Near-Human]]s who lacked physical [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], it was customary to hide their vestigial, empty sockets by wearing some kind of concealing headwear.<ref name="Miraluka">{{TORcite|type=codex|Miraluka}}</ref> Those headgears often took the form of a decorative veil,<ref name="The Sith Lords" /> a mask or a simple [[Leather/Legends|leather]] band.<ref name="Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> An extreme case of modesty, the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] of Tatooine were wrapped in strips of cloth and robe from head to foot, and the removal of clothing was strictly forbidden outside of intimacy with one's mate or certain rituals.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Because they had developed a strong exoskeleton, the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] of [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] had a phobia of exposed skin, and would avoid seeing it in others whenever possible.<ref name="FF16">{{FactFile|16|PLA 9-12|Planets of the Inner Rim}}</ref>

[[File:Selestrine1.jpg|thumb|left|170px|Depending on a culture's definition of modesty, certain types of clothing hid very little.]]
By contrast, some indigenous cultures were more relaxed on issues of modesty and clothing. The [[Icarii]] [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Selestrine]] was virtually nude, which would have been unthinkable on worlds like Naboo or [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 90" /> Similarly, [[Aron Peacebringer]] and his wife [[Alisande]], the planetary leaders of [[Shiva IV]], wore clothes that covered little more than their private parts.<ref name="LGA">[[Star Wars (1977) 53|''Star Wars'' (1977) 53]]</ref> Among the [[Fallanassi/Legends|Fallanassi]], adepts of the [[White Current/Legends|White Current]], it was uncontroversial for a woman to wear only a sarong, leaving her [[Breast/Legends|chest]] exposed.<ref name="Tyrants Test">''[[Tyrant's Test]]''</ref> Revealing clothes were common among [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] females, even individuals of respectable stations in life such as [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]]<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> or [[senatorial aide]]s.<ref name="Pampy">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/explore/attack/2003/03/imageattack20030328.html|series=Image Attack|text=Cerulean Aide}}</ref> The [[Witches of Dathomir|Witches]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] would strip and bathe in front of strangers in a detached, businesslike way, without the slightest intent to entice.<ref name="CoPL" />

For many furry species, nudity was no issue. The [[Yuzzem]]s of [[Ragna III]], the [[Drall/Legends|Dralls]] of [[Drall (planet)|Drall]],<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> the [[Sneevel/Legends|Sneevels]]<ref name="PT">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref> from [[Sneeve/Legends|Sneeve]]<ref name="DBBR">{{DB|character|bolesroor|Roor, Boles}}</ref> and the [[Yuzzum/Legends|Yuzzums]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]],<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> to name only a few, usually remained naked. Among the [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]], it was equally common to move about fully clothed<ref name="The Sith Lords" /><ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="SWR 49">[[Republic 49|''Republic'' 49]]</ref> or completely naked, even in the presence of other races.<ref name="gal">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> As similar observation could be made about the [[Defel/Legends|Defels]]<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref><ref name="SWHS" /> and the [[Elom/Legends|Eloms]].<ref name="SWR65">[[Republic 65|''Republic'' 65]]</ref><ref name="ROJ0">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Although reptilian, the [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] would go about their business unclothed on their homeworld of [[Gravlex Med/Legends|Gravlex Med]],<ref name="G7">{{GamerCite|7|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Anx}}</ref> while their representatives on Coruscant wore flowing robes.<ref name="FF 86">{{FactFile|86|RYY 1-2|Horox Ryyder}}</ref>

Sometimes, clothes were even specifically conceived to accentuate certain body parts, in order to seduce and to appeal to carnal desire. [[Slavery/Legends|Slave]] girls, masseuses, dancers and [[Prostitute/Legends|prostitutes]] were often dressed in such provocative clothes, which included [[Sensua binding/Legends|sensua bindings]], form-fitting [[Body glove/Legends|szona body gloves]]<ref name="SWV" /> and [[Tromin unigarment]]s.<ref name="TPMV" /> Microgarments, articles of clothing which were normally worn next to the skin and under other clothing for support, were also considered sexually appealing when worn alone.<ref name="The Sith Lords" />

===For fashion's sake===
[[File:My_poor_dress.png|thumb|right|180px|A group of well-meaning Zeltron trying to turn of Leia Organa's robe into something more "fashionable"]]
{{Quote|Keep your chin up, Leia. Maybe no one will notice.''"<br />"''They'll notice.''"<br />"''I'll bet.|Han Solo and Leia Organa, when the Princess was forced to wear a revealing robe|<ref name="SW95" />}}
All species and conditions considered, certain individuals attached a great deal of importance to the ever-changing concept of "fashion," a popular way of dressing restricted to a particular time or area. The [[Zeltron/Legends|Zeltrons]], who were often stereotyped as frivolous pleasure-seekers, were highly fashion-sensitive. They would not only dress in revealing apparel and bright shades,<ref name="FF134GAR17-18">{{FactFile|134|GAR 17-18|Garments and Couture}}</ref> but they were also willing to share their gusto with strangers. The Princess Leia Organa learned that lesson the hard way when a foursome of enthusiastic male Zeltrons transformed one of her sober Alderaanian white gowns into a much more gaudy attire, much to her dismay.<ref name="SW95" />

Even among the species who normally wore no clothes at all, some individuals did it for mere fashion purpose. Such was the case, for example, of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], a species of large gastropods. Individuals such as [[Malta]] and [[Embra]] were known to don short capes.<ref name="YV1">[[Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika 1|''Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika'' 1]]</ref> Many others distinguished themselves by wearing various types of headgear, including bell-shaped hats,<ref name="HuttCartel">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''</ref> berets,<ref name="EP">{{TCW|Evil Plans}}</ref> cylinder-shaped hats with a hanging tassel<ref name="FOSE3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 3]]</ref> or skullcaps.<ref name="SWL41">[[Legacy (2006) 41|''Legacy'' (2006) 41]]</ref> Some also used clothes to hide their infirmities, such as [[Oruba/Legends|Oruba]], who wrapped himself in an expansive shawl to conceal his diseased, cracking skin.<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{SWE|characters|oruba-the-hutt|Oruba the Hutt}}</ref> [[Jool]], a Hutt with a female personality, used to squeeze her wide torso into a laced corset to make it appear slimmer.<ref name="Leg 0">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref>

At the other end of the spectrum, some individuals had a complete lack of fashion acumen. The famous Corellian [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], never stood out as a stylish dresser. He rarely wore anything other than his trademark white shirt, black waistcoat, and brown pants,<ref name="FF134GAR17-18" /> and he considered dressing up a chore.<ref name="Union">''[[Star Wars: Union]]''</ref>

==Droids and clothing==
[[File:C3POInDress.png|thumb|left|160px|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] wearing [[Meg Pitareeze]]'s dress]]As [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were made to be resistant to higher or lower temperatures, they didn't need to wear clothes. However, some of them adopted clothing, either because of a personality quirk in their programming, or because it was ordered by their masters.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] had his [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] wear cloaks and headcloth made of [[Mumuu/Legends|mumuu]] hides. These clothes paid tribute to the ones worn by Grievous' former [[Izvoshra/Legends|Izvoshra]] elite warriors, when the general served as a [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] on his homeworld of [[Kalee/Legends|Kalee]].<ref name="ROSV" />

[[F8GN]], a droid owned by [[Garris Shrike]], would don Corellian street clothes in order to train Shrike's "rescued" children how to pickpocket. [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], who was once one of Shrike's orphans, used to think the spindly robot looked funny in clothes.<ref name="TPS" />

Some owners would have their droid servants wear a kerchief emblazoned with their emblem or that of an organization, like the Rebel agent [[Wyl Tarson]] did on his protocol unit [[T-2H4]] when he infiltrated the [[Raze's organization|organization]] of the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Raze (criminal)|Raze]].<ref name="SW:R6">[[Rebellion 6|''Rebellion'' 6]]</ref>

During his service on [[Kalarba/Legends|Kalarba]], [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] once served as a clothes horse for his mistress [[Meg Pitareeze]], while [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] was tending to her party dress. Unbeknownst to him, the golden droid was in fact striking a blow for droid rights: his donning Human clothes was interpreted as a voluntary fashion statement and became a pivotal moment in droid history. Later on, he was regarded as something of a hero in some droid circles, as he proved that machines too had an identity that could be expressed by clothing.<ref name="FF134GAR17-18" />
